header: Fat_CreateDirEntry(file, path): creates the directory entry of a file being opened for writing: finds a free slot (first name byte 0x00 or 0xE5) in the root directory (single-component path; vol +28 start, +44 entries; HL = 16 when full) or in the subdirectory the lookup left in +42, extending that directory with a zeroed cluster (Fat_AllocateClusters(file, 1, 1)) when its chain ends; it then fills the in-memory entry (slot +51, 8.3 name +52, attribute +64 = 0, first cluster +69 = 0, size +71 = 0), lets the device stamp the time +65 (block op 6), packs it into the sector (SeqStep_FileSectorReturn) and marks the sector dirty. Basis: callers + body -- the open slot SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer calls it only when Fat_LookupPath returned 5 (not found) and handle +3 bit 7 is set.

header: Fat_LookupPath(file, path): resolves the path to its directory entry and loads it into the handle. First asks the device (block op 7) whether the medium changed and, if so, drops its sectors from the 10-entry cache at 0x2121A (HL = 6 when one is dirty) and sets device +2 bit 1; then walks the 8.3 components (FatPath_Next83Component), comparing 11-byte names in the root directory and then in each subdirectory cluster chain, loading a match with SeqStep_FileSectorComplete (slot +51, first cluster +69 -> +42, Fat_CountContiguousClusters). HL = 0, 11 bad name, 12 component not a directory, 7 path not found, 5 file not found, 13 directory/file kind mismatch with handle +3 bit 6, 14 read-only entry opened writable (+3 bit 1), or a sector-cache error. Basis: callers + body -- the open slot SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer calls it first and treats 5 as "create" (Fat_CreateDirEntry).
evidence: sequencer/smf_event_processor.s:6592 `calr SeqByteBlock_PathNormalize_Helper6_Helper` / 6594 `ld iz, hl` -- caller SeqByteBlock_ChannelContainer (the open slot), result tested at 6598-6601

why_refused: The real caller (the `call` at midi/midi_dispatch_handlers.s:13807) is SeqData_FormatOutput_Default, entry 28 of SeqData_Handlers -- the received-SysEx command dispatch of SeqData_DispatchHandler -- not CaseC as the batch listed; neither name nor any header says what command 28 is. Body: decodes a 21-bit size (message +9..+11) and a 21-bit address (+6..+8, 7 bits per byte), rejects size <= 120 or address 0, reduces the address modulo 0x4000 and reads the byte at (that offset + 0x10) to choose a bound (type 0: offset+size <= 0x1D6, type 0x80: <= 0x2927, 0x40/0xC0: reject), then forwards the message to the sub CPU with sendCOMM (command 3) and returns 0, else 1 (the caller then queues F0 50 29 7E F7). What the address space is and why a low-RAM byte classifies it is not established, so "forward bulk data to the sub CPU" would overclaim the check it applies.

why_refused: Its only caller is SoundEvt_LongPacketHandler_DispatchTbl_Target1, entry 1 of SoundEvt_ModeDispatch_Tbl (display mode 1), a placeholder name with no header. Body: when bit 2 of 0x0D54 is set it clears it and, if the event at the cursor is a note-on (0x9n), sends note-offs (VoiceCtrl_SendNoteOffSequence), saves slot state 0, appends five bytes to the sequence buffer (four from VoiceSlot_FinalRetZ, then (0x0EEE) - 1), restores the slot, sets 0x28B3 bit 6 and 0x0F54 bit 0 and runs VoiceAlloc_ScoopDisplayProcess. What the five-byte record and the 0x0D54 bit 2 request are is not established (earlier batches refused the neighbouring 0x0D54/0x8D88 code for the same reason).
